messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Medical History:
The patient is a 20-year-old previously healthy male who presented to the emergency department with fever and rash six days after being diagnosed with a viral upper respiratory infection at an urgent care center.

Hospital Course:
The patient was diagnosed with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for supportive care. He required escalating amounts of supplemental oxygen during his ED course and remained hospitalized for 6 days.

Clinical Findings:
The patient presented with a diffuse, morbilliform rash across the trunk and extremities, sparing the face. A chest radiograph showed bilateral infiltrates consistent with multifocal pneumonia. Labs revealed a normal leukocyte count with an elevated C-reactive protein.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient received supportive care in the ICU, including supplemental oxygen and monitoring of vital signs.

Follow-up:
The patient is stable on hospital day 6 and will require additional monitoring and follow-up to determine the appropriate plan for discharge from the hospital.

Recommendations:
The patient should continue to follow up with his healthcare provider and monitor his symptoms closely to determine when he can safely return to his daily activities. Additionally, he should follow all recommendations and guidelines from public health officials regarding social distancing and hand hygiene to slow the spread of the virus.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The clinical picture (fever and rash about six days after a viral illness, a positive SARS-CoV-2 test, normal white cell count with raised CRP, and ICU-level multisystem involvement) points to multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults, not simple COVID-19 pneumonia. This is a post-infectious systemic inflammatory condition, classified under chapter M (musculoskeletal and connective tissue) as other systemic involvement of connective tissue, with SARS-CoV-2 coded as an additional condition.

CODE: M35
